Md Habibur Rahman, Advocate—For the Petitioners. 

Debashish Bhattachayrya with Md Arifur Rahman with Md Khorshedur Rahman with Najmul Karim with Mohammad Rafiqul Islam and Md Mazharul Islam Advocates—For the respondent No. 2.
parties:
Mizanur Rahman (Md) and others ---------- Petitioners
Vs.
Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd Court, Dhaka and another --------- Respondents
full_judgment:
"Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned order No. 7 dated 10-9-2015 and order No. 14 dated 18-1-2016 (Annexure-'C' and `C-1') passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Artha Execution Case No. 441 of 2014 arising out of Artha Rin Suit No. 42 of 2014 should not be declared to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect and/or why such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper." 

 3. Background leading to the Rule, in short, is that the Respondent No. 2, Eastern Bank Ltd., Dhaka as the plaintiff on 6-2-2014 instituted Artha Rin Case No. 42 of 2014 before the Artha Rin Adalat, 3rd Court, Dhaka (hereinafter referred to as Adalat) against the defendant petitioner for recovery of outstanding dues of Taka 11,38,472.92 (Eleven lac thirty eight thousand four hundred seventy two taka & ninety two paisa only). The Suit was decreed ex-parte on 22-6-. 2014 and put into execution in Artha Execution Case No. 441 of 2014. Thereafter, the petitioners submitted an application on 10-9-2010 before the Adalat to adjust the deposited amount under section 19(3) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as a Ain) by filing a Miscellaneous Case which was rejected by one of the impugned order and the plaintiff Bank also filed an application under section 34(7) read with section 57 of the Ain seeking warrant of arrest against the petitioner which was allowed by the second impugned order dated 15-4-2015 by issuing order of warrant of arrest against the petitioners and the petitioners deposited 25% equivalent to Taka 2,77,962 against decretal amount of Taka 11,38,472.95 in compliance with section 34(6) of the Ain and was enlarged on bail. The petitioner then filed an application to adjust the said deposit of 25% for treating the same as a deposit in terms of section 19(3) of the Ain and to register a Miscellaneous Case, which was of course rejected. 

 5. Mr Md Habibur Rahman, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner, after placing the petition, both the impugned orders and other materials on record mainly pressed his ground Nos. 5 and 6 of the petition and those grounds have been reflected in the factual matrices of the case as discussed above. He submits that the petitioners have already paid maximum amount against the principal loan amount, but the learned trial Court did not consider any of the submissions of the petitioners. The petitioners filed an application to adjust the money deposited during the time of obtaining bail asking to treat the deposit under section 19(3) of the Ain and to register the case as a Miscellaneous Case, but the trial Court did not consider this aspect and rejected the prayer, which is illegal in the eye of law. 

 6. Mr Debashis Bhattacaryya, the learned Advocate on the other hand appearing for the respondent No. 2, bank by filing vokalatnama entered appearance and opposed the Rule. His bone of contention is that the order of warrant of arrest which is order No. 7 dated 10-9-2015 (Annexure-C) does not suffer from any legal infirmity in as much as the same is absolutely in keeping with section 34 (9) and 10 of the Ain. There is no mortgaged property as it could be easily seen from the plaint of Execution case No. 441 of 2014 (Annexure-'A'). And in respect of second impugned order dated 18-1-2016 (Annexure-C1) the learned Counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the deposited 25% of the outstanding amount ought to have been treated as a legal deposit within the meaning of section 19(3) of the Ain but this aspect was not considered by the Adalat with positivity. The learned Counsel for the respondent, Mr. Debashis also candidly supported the submissions of the petitioner. 

 "It appears that the section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is clear and provides for ordering civil imprisonment up to 6 months against a judgment-debtor for compelling to satisfy the decree. Section-34 is not dependent upon section 33. In the instant case, the decree holder has taken step for auction sale of the property but there being no response, auction sale could not be held. Further it appears from the provisions of section 34 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 that the law provides for simple civil imprisonment of the judgment-debtor to compel to make the payment for satisfaction of the decree and is not an alternative punishment in lieu of payment of the decretal amount. Civil imprisonment will not exempt payment of the decretal amount." 

 13. We are in respectful agreement with the decision of Provat Kumar's case and hold that the said decision fortified what we have already discussed on the issue. 

 15. The ratio of Provat Kumar's case by now has been applied in several subsequent decisions. In a recent decision of Manik K. Bhattachayrya vs Artha Rin Adalat, (16 BLC 195) High Court Division has elaborated principle of civil imprisonment under section 34 of the Ain after discussing several decisions including Provat Kumar's case. 

 19. "Boni judicio est ampliare Jurisdictional" is a maxim which means it is the duty of a good Judge to extend Jurisdiction or in other words to enlarge his jurisdiction. But it does not necessarily mean that in course of interpretation a Judge would formulate any law but certainly a Judge can extend it's jurisdiction in a fit case. 

 20. On a plain reading of section 19(3) of the Ain we have found that for a registration of a Miscellaneous Case to set aside an ex-parte decree, it is required to deposit 10% of the decreetal amount either by cash or bank draft, pay order or by other method permissible under Negotiable Instrument Act as security. On the other hand the petitioner deposited 25% of the outstanding amount under section 34(6) of the Ain which is much more then the decretal amount. The petitioners for the purpose of releasing himself, under section 34(6) deposited 25% of the outstanding amount and was enlarged on bail. Therefore, by legal fiction we can hold that he has also deposited more then 10% as required under section 19(3) of the Ain. The law is clear that 10% of the decreetal amount is needed to register a Miscellaneous Case under section 19(3) of the Ain. Unhesitatingly, we can hold that it was absolutely a legal deposit to meet up legal necessity within the meaning of section 19(3) of the Ain. The deposit must be treated as a valid one under the same provision of law. 

 21. Even when we act in 'Ex debito justitiae' it is well justified to hold that the deposit was a legal deposit and perfect in all respect and the petitioner was entitled to have the Miscellaneous Case registered under section 19 of the Ain to set aside the ex-parte decree. 

 22. That being the situation, we are of the view that this Rule should be made absolute in part. The order No. 14 dated 18-1-2016 Annexure-C1 refusing to register the Miscellaneous Case is declared to have been passed without any lawful authority having no legal effect and set aside. The Adalat is directed to register immediately the Miscellaneous Case of the petitioner and dispose of the same in accordance with law forthwith.
